notes.unit: One row is an origin - a school (小/中/高 only) or a station. Everything is measured outward from it over the project's own segment network, in metres of riding rather than straight line.
notes.calm: The calm surface may only use segments at LTS 2 or below - the same definition score_network.R uses for a low-stress island, so an origin's calm reach is a distance-limited slice of the island it sits on. It is a subgraph, not a preference: a calm reach can never be a high-stress path that happens to end calmly.
notes.severed: population_any minus population_calm: residents who can reach this origin within the band, but not without riding a high-stress street. Both sides use the same buffer, mesh and graph, so severed_share is robust where the absolute counts are order-of-magnitude - quote the share.
notes.population: A 250m mesh cell counts in full when a usable street comes within 150m of its centroid, and not at all otherwise. Deliberately binary: area-weighting would imply we know how a cell's residents are distributed inside it, and the mesh is the finest thing e-Stat publishes.
notes.frontier: Corridors on the edge of the calm surface, capped at 8 per origin (frontier_corridor_count is the number before the cap; the ones dropped are the shortest). Only corridors whose own modelled after-state is low-stress appear - a crossing improvement has no modelled after-state at all, so it can never be credited with an unlock.
notes.unlock: The calm surface recomputed with that corridor's segments treated as low-stress, minus the calm surface as it stands. A counterfactual in the same sense as suitability_after, and inheriting its limits: it assumes the intervention is built as 05d modelled it, and models nothing about junctions, gradient or one-way streets.
